entry.author: City Rail Link
entry.summary:
How do you build New Zealand’s biggest transport infrastructure project?  
We’re taking you behind the scenes of the incredible story of the City Rail Link in a special five-part video series.
Episode two features the engineering giant that made it all possible – our tunnel boring machine.
Longer than a rugby field, weighing 910 tonnes, with a 7.15-metre diameter, and capable of housing 12 people inside, this engineering marvel excavated Auckland beneath the city streets. Along the way it helped install the concrete tunnel lining and remove thousands of tonnes of spoil, using more than 64,200 cubic metres of concrete – enough to fill 25 Olympic-sized swimming pools.
Take a look back at the machine that carved the path for Auckland’s rail future and the spectacular tunnel breakthroughs.
